config.title: Event Typing

intro.title: Event Typing
intro.body: In this lesson, you will build a simple Angular component that handles user input events, such as button clicks and text input, with proper TypeScript typing. You will learn how to use Angular's event binding syntax to capture events and define typed event handler methods. The core programming concept is event typing, which ensures your event handlers receive correctly typed data, improving code safety and developer experience. You'll work with Angular templates, TypeScript interfaces, and event objects like MouseEvent and KeyboardEvent. By the end, you'll create a responsive form that logs typed event details to the console.
intro.usecase: Event typing is essential in Angular applications where user interactions drive complex business logic. In e-commerce checkout forms, typed events ensure quantity selectors, shipping options, and payment method changes are handled with correct data types. Dashboard filtering controls rely on typed keyboard and mouse events to validate search inputs and update data visualizations accurately. Interactive admin panels use typed drag-and-drop events to manage content ordering while maintaining type safety across components.

objectives: Apply TypeScript interfaces to define custom event types for Angular components
Implement typed event emitters with explicit event payloads in child components
Bind typed event handlers in parent component templates to receive and process event data
Construct event handler methods that properly type the incoming event parameter
Initialize component state based on typed events received from child components
Render dynamic UI updates triggered by typed events with correct data flow
Manipulate event objects to extract and validate typed payload data

steps.title: Import Component and CommonModule from Angular core
steps.instruction: Import Component from '@angular/core' and CommonModule from '@angular/common' to prepare for creating an Angular component.
steps.hint: Use the import statement to bring in these Angular modules. Component is needed for the @Component decorator, and CommonModule provides common directives like ngIf and ngFor.
steps.expectedOutcome: The imports are added at the top of the file, making Component and CommonModule available for use in the component.
successCriteria: Component is imported from '@angular/core' and CommonModule is imported from '@angular/common'.
steps.feedbackCorrect: Nice! Proceed to the next step.
steps.feedbackPartial: You've imported one of the required modules, but both Component and CommonModule are needed. Check that you're importing from the correct packages.
steps.feedbackWrong: The imports are missing or incorrect. Remember to import Component from '@angular/core' and CommonModule from '@angular/common'.

steps.title: Create the main component class with TypeScript
steps.instruction: Create a component class named EventTypingComponent and decorate it with @Component.
steps.hint: Define a class with the name EventTypingComponent and add the @Component decorator above it.
steps.seedCode:
import { Component, CommonModule } from '@angular/core';

// Create the EventTypingComponent class with @Component decorator here
steps.expectedOutcome: A component class named EventTypingComponent is defined with the @Component decorator.
successCriteria: The EventTypingComponent class exists and is decorated with @Component.
steps.feedbackCorrect: Nice! Proceed to the next step.
steps.feedbackPartial: You're on the right track, but make sure the class is named EventTypingComponent and has the @Component decorator.
steps.feedbackWrong: The component class is missing or incorrectly defined. Check the class name and @Component decorator.

steps.title: Initialize component state with typed properties
steps.instruction: Inside the EventTypingComponent class, add two typed properties: 'message' (string) with initial value 'Click the button!' and 'clickCount' (number) with initial value 0.
steps.hint: Define properties directly in the class body using TypeScript type annotations and assign initial values.
steps.expectedOutcome: The component class now has two typed properties with initial values: message (string) and clickCount (number).
successCriteria: The EventTypingComponent class contains 'message: string = "Click the button!"' and 'clickCount: number = 0' as properties.
steps.feedbackCorrect: Nice! Proceed to the next step.
steps.feedbackPartial: You've added properties, but check that both have correct types and initial values: message should be a string with value 'Click the button!' and clickCount should be a number starting at 0.
steps.feedbackWrong: The component doesn't have the required typed properties. Make sure to add both 'message' and 'clickCount' with proper TypeScript type annotations and initial values inside the class body.

steps.title: Define a typed event handler method
steps.instruction: Inside the EventTypingComponent class, create a method named handleClick that accepts a MouseEvent parameter and updates the clickCount property.
steps.hint: Remember to use TypeScript type annotation for the event parameter: (event: MouseEvent).
steps.expectedOutcome: The component will have a properly typed event handler method ready to be connected to UI events.
successCriteria: The handleClick method is defined with a MouseEvent parameter type and increments clickCount.
steps.feedbackCorrect: Nice! Proceed to the next step.
steps.feedbackPartial: You've created the method, but check that it properly accepts a MouseEvent parameter and updates clickCount.
steps.feedbackWrong: The handleClick method is missing or doesn't match the required signature. Review the instruction.

steps.title: Add basic template structure with event binding
steps.instruction: In the component's template, add a button element with the text 'Click me' and bind its click event to the handleClick method using Angular's (click) syntax.
steps.hint: Use the (click)="handleClick()" attribute on a <button> element inside the template string.
steps.analogousExample:
// Example: button with event binding in Angular template
<button (click)="onButtonClick()">Click me</button>
steps.expectedOutcome: The component's template now contains a button that will trigger the handleClick method when clicked.
successCriteria: The template includes a <button> element with the text 'Click me' and uses (click)="handleClick()" event binding.
steps.feedbackCorrect: Nice! Proceed to the next step.
steps.feedbackPartial: You're close. Make sure you have a button element with the correct text and the (click) binding to handleClick().
steps.feedbackWrong: The template doesn't contain the required button with event binding. Check that you added a <button> with (click)="handleClick()" inside the template.

steps.title: Display component state in the template
steps.instruction: In the component's template, add interpolation to display the message and clickCount properties. Use double curly braces {{ }} to show each property's value.
steps.hint: Interpolation syntax in Angular templates is {{ propertyName }}. You'll need to reference the component's properties inside the template.
steps.expectedOutcome: The template will show the current values of message and clickCount when the component renders.
successCriteria: The template contains interpolation expressions {{ message }} and {{ clickCount }} to display the component's properties.
steps.feedbackCorrect: Nice! Proceed to the next step.
steps.feedbackPartial: You're on the right track, but make sure you're using the correct interpolation syntax {{ }} and referencing the component's properties by name.
steps.feedbackWrong: The template doesn't yet display the component's state. Remember to use interpolation syntax {{ propertyName }} to show property values in Angular templates.

steps.title: Add input field with keyboard event typing
steps.instruction: Inside the template, add an input element with (keyup) event binding to a handleKeyUp method. Include a placeholder attribute with text like 'Type something'.
steps.hint: Use the (keyup) event binding syntax and create a placeholder attribute for the input field.
steps.analogousExample:
// Example: input with keyboard event
<input (keyup)="handleKeyUp($event)" placeholder="Enter text here">
steps.expectedOutcome: The template will contain an input field that triggers a keyboard event handler when keys are released.
successCriteria: An input element with (keyup) event binding to handleKeyUp method and a placeholder attribute is present in the template.
steps.feedbackCorrect: Nice! Proceed to the next step.
steps.feedbackPartial: You're on the right track, but make sure you have both the (keyup) event binding and a placeholder attribute in your input element.
steps.feedbackWrong: The input element is missing or doesn't have the required (keyup) event binding and placeholder attribute. Check the syntax and try again.

steps.title: Add form submission with form event typing
steps.instruction: Add a form element in the template with (submit) event binding that calls a handleSubmit method.
steps.hint: Use the <form> tag with (submit)="handleSubmit($event)" and include a submit button inside.
steps.analogousExample:
// Form with typed event handler
<form (submit)="onFormSubmit($event)">
  <button type="submit">Submit</button>
</form>
steps.expectedOutcome: The component template will include a form element with proper event binding for submission.
successCriteria: A form element with (submit) event binding to handleSubmit is added to the template.
steps.feedbackCorrect: Nice! Proceed to the next step.
steps.feedbackPartial: You added a form, but make sure it has (submit)="handleSubmit($event)" binding.
steps.feedbackWrong: Try adding a <form> element with (submit) event binding that calls handleSubmit.

steps.title: Define form event handler with Event type
steps.instruction: In your EventTypingComponent class, define a method named handleSubmit that takes an Event parameter and calls preventDefault() on it.
steps.hint: Remember to add the Event type annotation to the method parameter. The method should prevent the default form submission behavior.
steps.expectedOutcome: You should have a handleSubmit method that properly types the event parameter and prevents default form submission behavior.
successCriteria: The handleSubmit method is defined with an Event parameter type and calls preventDefault() on it.
steps.feedbackCorrect: Nice! Proceed to the next step.
steps.feedbackPartial: You're close! Make sure your handleSubmit method has the correct Event type parameter and calls preventDefault().
steps.feedbackWrong: The handleSubmit method is missing or doesn't match the required signature. It should accept an Event parameter and call preventDefault().
